title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: The page continues a lemma started on the previous page. C is a category and A a full subcategory. f: C → Â = Hom(A°, Ens) is the restricted Yoneda functor X ↦ Hom(−, X)|_A. In the additive case, f_ab: C → Â_ab sends X to the additive presheaf Hom(−, X)|_A on A. Previous page: if every X is the colimit in C of a diagram in A (canonically, X ≃ colim over A/X), then f is fully faithful. So is f_ab, since the forgetful functor Â_ab → Â is faithful. This page: suppose every object is a colimit of a given type (e.g. finite sums) of objects of A. Then the essential image of C lies in the presheaves that are such colimits of representables. In the additive case one must interpret this using the 'half-addition' structure on A: A is not closed under sums, but it inherits an Ab-enrichment, i.e. a preadditive structure, from its embedding in the additive category C. If moreover C is stable under that type of colimit, one gets an equivalence between C and the category of presheaves (Ens- or Ab-valued) on A that are such colimits of representables. The worked case: C additive, every object a finite direct sum of objects of A. Then C is equivalent to the full subcategory of Â_ab (additive contravariant functors A → Ab) formed by finite direct sums of representables. Equivalently, C is the additive envelope of the preadditive category A. The next page specialises to A = {single object} with endomorphism ring k: C is then equivalent to finitely generated free right k-modules via X ↦ Hom(A, X). The next page then dualises (covariant functors, limits). In context this is a formal tool for the main project, the dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. It describes additive categories of 'free' or 'perfect' objects as module-like categories over a generating subcategory: Morita-type reduction to rings with several objects.
errors: The general claim that, when every X is a colimit of some type of objects of A, the image of X in Â is the 'same type' of colimit of representables is false in general. The restricted Yoneda functor does not preserve colimits: e.g. in Ens-valued presheaves, Hom(Y, X ⊔ X') ≠ Hom(Y,X) ⊔ Hom(Y,X') in general. The claim holds for absolute colimits, notably finite direct sums (biproducts) in the additive case, which is the case Grothendieck actually works out.
The intended general equivalence needs this extra preservation hypothesis, not just 'C stable under that type of limits'. In the additive/finite-direct-sum case the statement is correct.
The example 'stable by finite products' fits the dual (covariant, projective limit) version on the next page better than the colimit version here; this is a minor slip.

ideas.what: Restricted Yoneda along a dense full subcategory is fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Dense subcategory / density theorem (nerve functor fully faithful)

ideas.what: Full subcategory of an additive category inherits a preadditive ('½ addition') structure; additive version of restricted Yoneda
ideas.modern_name: Preadditive category; additive Yoneda embedding into Mod-A

ideas.what: Additive C whose objects are finite direct sums of objects of A is equivalent to the finite sums of representables in additive presheaves on A; single object gives f.g. free End-modules
ideas.modern_name: Additive envelope / Morita-type equivalence, free modules over a ringoid

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard formal lemma (density, additive Yoneda, additive envelope / free modules over a ringoid) prepared as a tool. Only the idiosyncratic term 'structure ½ addition' for preadditive structure is mildly notable; there is no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'donc $A$ induit sur A une structure ½ addition' should read 'donc C induit sur A une structure ½ addition'.
'si ∀ objet de C' corresponds to 'si tout objet de C' in the manuscript.

The first lines likely read 'qui sont lim. du type envisagé de foncteurs représentables (dans le cas resp. ab utilisé, pour y donner un sens si C est additive... la structure "½ addition" sur A héritée par son plongement dans C additive)'.
In the struck passage, 'A est réduite à un objet' is plausible, but the remainder is illegible.
